data.content_ref: inline:KIND: contradiction. SRC_002 contradicts both SRC_001/SRC_004 and SRC_005 simultaneously and the disagreement is quantitative, not qualitative: all three agree the only absorbing obstructions are locally stable matchings and that cut size descends monotonically, so the consensus probability equals the basin weight of the empty cut, which is exactly 1 minus the total basin weight of stable matchings. SRC_005's expander-rarity argument is COMPATIBLE WITH SRC_001 if one distinguishes counting from reachability: stable matchings may be exponentially rare as static objects yet still absorb almost all dynamics trajectories, because the descent path itself manufactures them. I conjecture the neighbourhood summaries are all descriptions of the same object seen through three wrong lenses: the number of reachable stable matchings is Θ(n)·p_n for a per-edge trapping probability p_n, and the whole dispute reduces to whether p_n decays (SRC_005), stabilizes (SRC_002), or is offset by Θ(n) opportunities (SRC_001). It is REFUTED IF one can exhibit a single random 3-regular graph and update schedule where the descent passes through a non-matching non-consensus local minimum, since that would break the shared premise all candidates inherit from SRC_001's monotone-descent mechanism.
